neighbours.label: A roll/turn verb in a reversal phrase predicting 'back' (roll back, turn back, no turning back), vs the same reversal stated with another verb
fire: The board voted to roll back the price increase after protests.
Once the papers were signed, there was no turning back.
Engineers had to roll back the update when the servers crashed.
The storm forced the climbers to turn back below the summit.
Critics say the bill would roll back decades of environmental rules.
Halfway across the bridge she felt the urge to turn back.
The council later rolled back its ban on street vendors.
After the first lie, he felt there was no turning back.
quiet: The board voted to cancel the price increase after protests.
Once the papers were signed, the deal was final.
Engineers had to undo the update when the servers crashed.
The storm forced the climbers to stop below the summit.
Critics say the bill would weaken decades of environmental rules.
Halfway across the bridge she felt the urge to stop.
The council later lifted its ban on street vendors.
After the first lie, he felt the deception was permanent.

predictions: roll/turning before 'back' reaches 0.4-0.75; the same sentences with reverse/undo/cancel stay under 0.15. Literal 'rolls a marble' sits near 0.3.
notes: Card: ' roll' x3, 'roll' x2, ' rolled' x2 (roll it back, roll back improvements), 'no turning back', 'look into'. Probe: 'no turning back' 0.719, 'roll back the reforms' 0.537, 'rolls a marble' 0.299, 'roll their own' 0.083, 'reverse the reforms' 0.083, 'egg roll' 0.012.
